technique: 3D CGI built to emulate a felted stop-motion puppet look, not true frame-by-frame stop-motion. Skin and clothing show a fuzzy, fiber/wool-like surface texture (visible on the woman's mustard sweater and the man's dark coat, and even on the exposed 'skin' of the noses/faces), which is a rendered material rather than photographed felt grain -- there's no photographic sensor noise, dust, or fingerprint dents in the clay/felt that would confirm physical puppets. Adjacent periodic frames (periodic-4 through periodic-11, spanning roughly 3-9s of screen time) show continuous, interpolated micro-movement of the head, eyelids and mouth with no visible frame-holds or stepped jitter, which argues for CG rigging (or CG-assisted stop-motion post-processed to remove jitter) over handmade armature animation. Uncertainty flagged: without a wireframe or turntable shot it cannot be fully ruled out that this is real stop-motion with digital noise reduction, but the perfectly clean specular highlights on the glasses and ice cream cone, plus the razor-stable studio-quality lighting across cuts, point toward a CG pipeline.
facial_animation_notes: Faces are rigid felt-like blocks with painted-on eyebrows and a static thin-line mouth carved into the surface; when characters speak, the mouth opens into a simple dark oval cavity (see periodic-6 'REEL', periodic-9 'ALREADY', scene-2 'THIS') rather than shaping distinct visemes -- a limited/graphic mouth-shape library, not full lip sync. The man's mouth interpolates smoothly between closed smirk and open oval with no in-between jaw chatter, suggesting few keyframes per phoneme (a 'talking blob' approach) rather than dense per-frame mouth animation.
eye_and_blink_notes: Both characters have heavy-lidded, half-closed eyes as a resting expression (visible in almost every frame), giving a permanently unimpressed/deadpan look; no full blink is captured in any of the periodic frames, but the upper lid height visibly changes between frames (e.g. periodic-9 'GOD' shows the woman's eyes wide open and alert versus her half-lidded default in periodic-4/5/6), indicating the eyelids are an animated (rigged) shape rather than a fixed sculpt. Pupils are simple painted dots that shift slightly in the socket for gaze changes rather than fully rotating eyeballs.
head_movement_notes: The man's head performs a slow, continuous downward-tilting turn from screen-left (looking at the woman, periodic-3/4) toward frontal/upward (periodic-6 through periodic-9) over several seconds -- the transition is gradual and smooth across consecutive periodic frames with no sudden snaps or held poses, consistent with rigged interpolation rather than stop-motion's characteristic per-frame positional jumps. The woman's head stays comparatively static, tilted toward the phone, for most of the sequence, only lifting to look at the man in the later store-front shot (scene-2).
gesture_notes: Hand/arm poses are essentially locked for the whole outdoor dialogue block: the woman holds her phone at chest height with minimal repositioning across all periodic frames, and the man holds his ice cream cone in a fixed low position throughout -- neither arm gesticulates to punctuate the dialogue. The only gesture-level change visible is a slight forward tilt/raise of the phone between periodic-2 and periodic-3, suggesting gestures were animated sparsely and held for multiple lines rather than continuously re-animated.
idle_motion_notes: No secondary idle motion (breathing chest movement, cloth sway, hair sway) is visible between frames -- the fuzzy sweater and coat surfaces stay geometrically identical frame to frame apart from the animated head/eye regions, indicating idle/rest body posture is essentially a locked pose while only the head, eyes and mouth carry performance animation.
frame_rate_feel: Source video is 30fps per metadata.json, and motion across adjacent periodic keyframes reads as smooth/interpolated rather than choppy -- there is no visible stepped or held-frame stutter typical of on-2s stop-motion; the perceived feel is a steady, continuous crawl of small facial/head adjustments, i.e. animated closer to the native frame rate (or with dense enough keyframes) that no discrete stair-stepping is detectable at this sampling interval.
overall_animation_style_notes: A deadpan, low-amplitude performance style: two long-nosed, felt-textured character designs seated/standing almost motionlessly through a multi-line joke, relying on minimal, slow head turns and subtle eyelid/mouth changes rather than broad gesture or body acting to sell the humor. The restraint (locked torsos, fixed props in hand, sparse eye widening only at punchline beats like 'GOD' and 'ALREADY') suggests a deliberately economical animation style where comedic timing is carried by voice performance and on-screen caption text more than by physical animation.
